doc.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997

title: His Italian grandfather, the tuba player who nearly joined Sousa
summary: His tailor grandfather played tuba in concert and parade bands, was wanted by Sousa but stayed home, and took young Nick to hear the bands.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: The grandfather you mentioned, was he the one that played with John Phillip Sousa?

Yes. How that came about was he was not a — my grandfather was born in Italy and he was a musician first. And then when he got married and came to the United States he had to support a family so he became a tailor. And he played gigs on the side. And a few times he was called to play with the Sousa band. And Sousa wanted him to, you know, be part of the — he was a great tuba player. And my grandmother said no dice, you know, you’d better stay home and make a living. So he wound up actually still being a great musician staying home. He wound up playing tuba in marching bands and concert bands, which I used to go with him all the time. He always used to take me to hear these old, like Italian concert bands and parade bands. So he was kind of my idol. When I grew up I wanted to put on a uniform and march in a parade. And you know he was always encouraging me to play music.
